lines: +Exposed more UI parts and states as themable CSS custom properties. You can now restyle them on `:root` (or `:host` in a shadow root), and every token defaults to its current value, so the default theme renders unchanged.

+* Toolbar: the border and radius of the toolbar's own buttons in every toolbar (`--ck-toolbar-button-border`, `--ck-toolbar-button-border-radius`), including compact toolbars, toolbars in dropdown panels, and open dropdown and split buttons in toolbars, and the separator width (`--ck-toolbar-separator-width`). The button tokens do not reach lists in dropdown panels.
+* Form header and dialog header: the background and text color (`--ck-form-header-background`, `--ck-form-header-text-color`, `--ck-dialog-header-background`).

+* Dropdown: the gap between the label and the arrow (`--ck-dropdown-arrow-gap`). The open dropdown button radius (`--ck-dropdown-panel-uniform-button-border-radius`) now defaults to `--ck-button-border-radius`.
+* Split button and list: the separator width and height (`--ck-split-button-separator-width`, `--ck-list-separator-height`).
+* List item button: the text color and hover background of a toggleable item in the "on" state (`--ck-list-item-button-on-text-color`, `--ck-list-item-button-on-hover-background`).
+* Tab button: the focus border color and the label color of the active tab (`--ck-tab-button-focus-border-color`, `--ck-tab-button-active-text-color`).
+* Insert table grid: the cell border, and the background and border of selected cells and of the cell under the pointer (`--ck-insert-table-dropdown-box-*`).
+* Heading dropdown: the label width and the list item minimum width (`--ck-heading-dropdown-label-width`, `--ck-heading-dropdown-list-item-min-width`).
+* Find and replace: the result and selected result background and text color (`--ck-find-result-*`). The legacy `--ck-color-find-result-selected` keeps working.

+* Code block: the language label background and text color (`--ck-code-block-label-background`, `--ck-code-block-label-text-color`). The legacy `--ck-color-code-block-label-background` keeps working.
+* Style grid: the border of the selected style and of the selected style under the pointer (`--ck-style-panel-button-on-border-color`, `--ck-style-panel-button-on-hover-border-color`).

All tokens are defined and resolved on `:root`, so a scoped override of a lower-layer token does not re-flow up through the chain. The closer a token sits to the property it controls, the better it works when scoped - which makes component tokens the safe choice for per-element tweaks. Legacy token names are an exception: the theme reads them at each point of use, so a legacy override also works when scoped - the {@link updating/migration-to-refreshed-theme migration guide} covers the few re-themed tokens that stay `:root`-only.

+To restyle the buttons of every toolbar without touching other buttons, use the toolbar button tokens. They apply to the buttons of the editor toolbar, balloon and widget toolbars, compact toolbars in forms (for example the alignment toolbar in table properties), and toolbars in dropdowns:
+Scope them to one toolbar to restyle only its buttons:

+A scoped override also reaches the toolbars in dropdown panels opened from that toolbar, for example the alignment toolbar or the "Show more items" toolbar, because they are toolbars too. Lists in dropdown panels keep their regular button styles. To give the toolbars in dropdown panels the regular button styles, unset the tokens there. This also drops any value you set for the toolbar tokens on `:root`:

+Until you set them, toolbar buttons use `--ck-button-border` and `--ck-button-border-radius`. The outer corners of compact toolbars, for example in table properties, use `--ck-border-radius-control`.

+An open dropdown or split button in a toolbar also uses `--ck-toolbar-button-border-radius`, ahead of `--ck-dropdown-panel-uniform-button-border-radius`. If you set both, for example `--ck-dropdown-panel-uniform-button-border-radius: initial` to keep the attached-corner look, the toolbar button radius wins for open dropdowns in toolbars. The vertical toolbar keeps its own `--ck-toolbar-vertical-button-border-radius`.
* Override the **closest** token to what you want to change; drop to a lower layer only when the change should reach further.

+Names that start with `--_ck-` (with an underscore) are internal helpers, not tokens. The theme uses them to pass values between components without shadowing the public tokens, for example `--_ck-button-context-border`, which the toolbar sets on its own buttons. Do not set or read them in your theme. They are not part of the public API and may change or be removed in any release.

Naming is only half the story. For how to pick a layer and override tokens in practice - global versus scoped overrides and the per-element caveats - see the {@link framework/theme-customization Theme customization} guide.
+ * Custom properties prefixed with `--_ck-` (note the underscore) are internal helpers, not theming tokens. They let
+ * a component change what a button reads without redeclaring the public `--ck-button-*` tokens, which would shadow
+ * `:root` overrides. Do not set them in themes; they may change or be removed without notice. Two kinds exist:
+ * - `--_ck-button-fallback-*` sits after the public token, so it only changes the default and a theme still wins.
+ * - `--_ck-button-context-*` sits before the public token, so a container (for example the toolbar) can apply its own
+ *   token to the buttons it owns. The container sets it on those buttons only, to keep it out of nested panels
+ *   (a toolbar in a dropdown panel sets its own through the same rule).
